item.title: Adaptive Precision Incomplete Matrix Factorization
item.description: arXiv:2611.28235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Incomplete factorizations are widely used to precondition Krylov subspace methods for solving large sparse linear systems. Recent work has explored computing approximate factorizations in low precision, but using only one uniformly low precision limits the achievable accuracy and can degrade the quality of the preconditioner. We propose adaptive precision incomplete factorization algorithms in which we store each entry of the factors in a precision chosen according to its magnitude and a target accuracy. We present a rounding error analysis showing that the adaptive precision threshold-based incomplete LU and incomplete Cholesky factorizations achieve a backward error of the order of the target accuracy. We also discuss how to incorporate pivoting and scaling and how to perform the triangular solves with the adaptive precision factors. Finally, we explain how the approach applies to memory-limited incomplete Cholesky factorizations by using the magnitude of the largest dropped entry as the target accuracy. Numerical experiments on a wide range of matrices from the SuiteSparse collection show that adaptive precision can substantially reduce the storage required by the factors without degrading the quality of the preconditioner and improve the storage-weighted iteration count and overall storage required compared with uniform 64-, 32-, and 16-bit factorizations.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Lister, Theo Mary, Jennifer Scott

item.title: Sub-Riemannian flow matching
item.description: arXiv:2611.28433v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study sub-Riemannian conditional flow matching (SRCFM) for generative transport with prescribed velocity constraints. Training uses paths between sampled source and target points whose velocities lie in the allowed horizontal directions at each state. A neural network takes time and the full state as input and predicts the coefficients of these directions, and the horizontal frame then determines the full velocity used for generation. We describe constructions based on Heisenberg geodesics and joint endpoint equations in free step-two Carnot groups. We propose a scalable piecewise algorithm that computes horizontal paths directly from their endpoints. A straight segment sets the horizontal coordinates, and a loop in those coordinates corrects the remaining vertical displacement. We verify the algorithm's endpoint accuracy to numerical precision in high-dimensional tests. Synthetic experiments illustrate approximate distribution transport along horizontal trajectories. On resized MNIST, we use the same construction to generate images from Gaussian inputs with fewer controls than pixels.
item.dc:creator: Wonjun Lee, Scott Zimmerman

item.title: Data-driven discovery of sparse governing equations with parameterized operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.28556v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study parameterized SINDy (pSINDy), an extension of the Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) framework for the discovery of parsimonious governing equations involving operators with unknown parameters such as fractional-order Caputo derivatives, fractional Laplacians, and parameterized kernel operators. The framework jointly identifies the unknown operator parameters and sparse library coefficients through a sparsity-promoting optimization problem. To solve this problem, we develop and analyze the parameterized sequentially thresholded least-squares (pSTLSQ) algorithm. In each iteration, it removes terms with small coefficients, updates the operator parameters by a fixed number of optimization steps that improve the fit of the remaining library terms, and refits their coefficients by least squares. Under suitable assumptions, we prove that pSTLSQ converges locally to a local minimizer and give sufficient conditions for identifying the terms present in the governing equation. Numerical experiments demonstrate recovery of governing equations from noisy synthetic data for fractional ODEs, fractional PDEs, and nonlocal diffusion equations. We also examine the influence of the hyperparameters, discretization scheme, and noise, and compare pSTLSQ with two benchmark methods. All three methods identify the correct terms at low noise levels, but differ in parameter accuracy, cost, and sensitivity to initialization and the candidate library.
item.dc:creator: Mike Wendels, J. Nathan Kutz

item.title: A hybrid high-order discretization of a volume integral formulation for eddy currents on unstructured polyhedral meshes
item.description: arXiv:2611.28557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Volume integral formulations are attractive for eddy-current simulation because they require a mesh only of the conducting region. However, their dense interaction matrices make it important to control the number of unknowns needed for a prescribed accuracy. We propose an arbitrary-order Hybrid High-Order discretization of a current-based volume integral formulation on general unstructured polyhedral meshes. The method combines high-order polynomial approximation with local mesh refinement around defects and material interfaces. For bounded positive spatially varying resistivity and magnetic permeability uniform throughout space, we establish well-posedness and a priori error estimates using a constructive right inverse of the discrete divergence. Numerical experiments demonstrate convergence for smooth solutions and compare mesh refinement with increasing the polynomial degree. Selected comparisons show that higher degree on coarser meshes can reduce the number of current unknowns coupled by the Green operator and the associated storage for a prescribed accuracy. Finally, a three-dimensional eddy-current testing benchmark assesses the predicted impedance against experimental measurements, using local refinement around a narrow slot and reusing the system matrix and its factorization throughout the probe scan.
item.dc:creator: Raman Kumar, Aurelio Spadotto, Silvano Pitassi

item.title: Deterministic regularisation of the nonsymmetric eigenproblem
item.description: arXiv:2611.28614v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a deterministic algorithm for pseudospectral shattering in exact arithmetic. This resolves an important open problem in the complexity of the nonsymmetric eigenproblem. Given a complex contraction $A$ of order $n\ge2$ and $0<\delta<1/2$, we compute a perturbation $E$ with $\|E\|<\delta$ such that $A+E$ has simple spectrum. The ratio of its eigenbasis condition number to its minimum eigenvalue gap is at most $C(n/\delta)^{20/3}$. The algorithm also computes an exact eigensystem of $A+E$. It uses $O(n^3\log^d(n/\delta))$ real-field operations and comparisons, where $C$ and $d$ are absolute constants. We choose the rank-one perturbations using a lower bound on the circle mean of the logarithm of the discriminant modulus. A quadratic penalty controls how far the accumulated updates move the matrix. By using the same reference eigenbasis for several updates, we can estimate all the current projector norms while recovering only the directions needed for the next perturbation.
item.dc:creator: Matthew J. Colbrook

item.title: Finite-difference neural policy iteration for high-dimensional degenerate Hamilton--Jacobi equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.28639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a finite-difference neural policy iteration method for high-dimensional degenerate Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman and Isaacs equations. Artificial viscosity yields a monotone finite-difference operator, and neural networks approximate the linear equations of semi-discrete policy iteration using local stencil values. This avoids global tensor-grid storage. For measurable feedbacks, we bound the propagation of evaluation, terminal, gradient, and control optimization errors by a geometrically weighted sum. Discrete comparison, consistency, and vanishing viscosity relate the approximation to the original degenerate equation. On coupled manufactured problems with rank-deficient diffusion, the method achieves lower mean errors than direct physics-informed neural networks at every tested dimension from five to fifty under equal training time. At fifty dimensions and $900$ seconds, the mean relative $L^2$ error over three paired seeds is about $40\%$ lower. Two-dimensional refinement attains $0.297\%$ error against the original degenerate solution, with independent grid references separating approximation error from viscosity bias. In a twenty-dimensional game with finite control sets, reusing policies reduces the measured time to a relative error of $5\%$ by $24.3\%$ compared with direct minimization of the same discrete residual with fresh samples at every update.
item.dc:creator: Hee Jun Yang, Yeoneung Kim

item.title: Numerical approximation of the Hilfer fractional derivative using orthogonal Quasi-Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.28643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A numerical approach based on a composite Gaussian quadrature for the Hilfer fractional derivative is presented. This approach employs quasi-polynomials that are orthogonal with respect to the weight function on the interval $(0,1)$. As special cases, the Riemann--Liouville and Caputo fractional derivatives are obtained. Error bounds for the approximation are derived. To confirm the convergence rates as well as the high efficiency of the new approach, numerical examples are provided.
item.dc:creator: Rabab Beirkdar, Swaminathan Anbhu

item.title: Quantitative Convergence of the Spherical Brownian Motion collisional particle system for the Maxwellian Landau Equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.28663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish the quantitative convergence of the spherical Brownian motion (SBM) collisional particle system for the Maxwellian Landau equation via Wasserstein distances. When used as numerical method, it enjoys linear complexity $O(N)$ in particle number $N$, and conserves the momentum and energy almost surely. Moreover, only random grouping and sampling are needed for simulations without further numerical discretization. In the first part, we identify the large particle mean field limit of the system, and the Wasserstein convergence to the limit is justified through a coupling similar to the recent work for the Nanbu type Monte Carlo method \cite{BorghiPareschi2025}. The key difference is that the particles in our coupled shadow system are not i.i.d. due to the perfect matching. In the second part, the convergence of the mean field dynamics to the Landau solution is justified by the relative entropy with a bound $O(\tau^2)$, being $\tau$ the stepsize. This results in an $O(\tau)$ bound for the Wasserstein distance error. A crucial technical tool in the convergence in relative entropy is to provide suitable bounds on the derivatives of the logarithmic density or score function in the mean field dynamics. The combination of these estimates leads to the full convergence of the squared Wasserstein distance with order $O(N^{-1/2}+\tau^2)$ for the numerical scheme in $d=3$.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Antonio Carrillo, Ruizhi Huang, Lei Li

item.title: Interface-aware dynamic mode decomposition with control for partitioned multiphysics systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.28668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an interface-aware dynamic mode decomposition with control (DMDc) formulation for multiphysics systems, within an optimization-based partitioned coupling framework. The finite-element interface-input operator is projected onto the reduced space and kept fixed during identification, while the unknown state-dependent local dynamics are learned from trajectory data. The common interface control is recomputed online by minimizing the mismatch between the reconstructed physical interface quantities. The formulation accommodates local subproblems governed by ordinary differential equations (ODEs) and differential--algebraic equations (DAEs). For a DAE subproblem, tangent projection identifies the state dynamics, whereas a residualized normal regression identifies the pressure balance and provides an algebraic pressure reconstruction. We further propose regularized quadratic correction DMDc to enrich the tangent dynamics and, for DAEs, the normal pressure balance through jointly fitted linear and compact quadratic operators. Feature normalization and block-dependent regularization control the enlarged regression while retaining the prescribed interface operators and identified DAE geometry. The proposed framework is evaluated on problems involving both ODE--ODE and DAE--ODE couplings. The numerical results demonstrate accurate predictions and stable long-time behavior.
item.dc:creator: Jiarui Tian, Dunhui Xiao, Lei Zhang

item.title: Well-balanced nodal finite volume WENO scheme with flux localization for hyperbolic balance laws
item.description: arXiv:2611.28678v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop a general framework for constructing arbitrarily high-order well-balanced ``nodal" finite volume weighted essentially non-oscillatory (WENO) schemes, specifically tailored for hyperbolic balance laws. To handle complex systems involving nonconservative products and steady-state solutions with global integral quantities, we introduce a flux localization technique. This technique defines the numerical fluxes, incorporating the entire source term and nonconservative products, locally within each computational cell. By exactly preserving the nodal equilibrium state and conservatively updating the cell averages within a finite volume framework, the method avoids both reference-state reconstruction and the use of ODE solvers. The well-balanced property is achieved by performing high-order WENO reconstruction and employing a linear segment path in terms of equilibrium variables, rather than conservative ones. A rigorous theoretical analysis confirms that the scheme exactly preserves all the targeted stationary solutions. The effectiveness and versatility of the proposed method are demonstrated through a series of numerical experiments on various systems of hyperbolic balance laws.
item.dc:creator: Jiahui Zhang, Yinhua Xia, Yan Xu

item.title: Structure-preserving active flux method for the compressible Euler equations with gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.28683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a structure-preserving active flux method for the compressible Euler equations under gravitational fields, ensuring exactness for the generalized hydrostatic equilibrium state and the preservation of positivity for both density and pressure. This approach entails the update of the cell average and the point values simultaneously. To obtain the equilibrium preservation of the scheme for the cell average, the strategy pursued is to reformulate the gravitational term using the steady state solution, followed by the application of a decomposition algorithm. For the point values, we introduce minor adjustments to the Lax-Friedrichs flux vector splitting, coupled with the same finite difference operator performed on the flux and source term to restore the well-balancedness. Furthermore, a posteriori Multi-dimensional Optimal Order Detection (MOOD) paradigm is adopted for achieving positivity preservation and oscillation control near strong discontinuities. A series of numerical experiments are performed to verify the high-order accuracy of our proposed method, along with its exact equilibrium and positivity preservation, and its ability to capture small perturbations at or close to steady flow without spurious oscillations.
item.dc:creator: Jiahui Zhang, Christian Klingenberg

item.title: Worst case tractability of weighted linear tensor product problems under the absolute error criterion
item.description: arXiv:2611.28789v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies weighted linear tensor product problems in the worst case setting. We consider algorithms that use finitely many evaluations of arbitrary continuous linear functionals. We investigate algebraic and exponential tractability under the absolute error criterion in the case $\lambda_1>1$, where $\lambda_1$ is the square of the univariate maximal singular value. We obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for various notions of algebraic and exponential tractability on weights and univariate singular values. Our approach is to convert algebraic tractability of the problems for the absolute error criterion with $\lambda_1 > 1$ to exponential tractability of the normalized problems. Specifically, we solve Open Problem 27 as posed by Novak and Wo\'zniakowski (2008).
item.dc:creator: Heping Wang, Yuheng Xi

item.title: Perturbed QMC designs and reduced QMC strength
item.description: arXiv:2611.28831v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Small errors in sampling locations can change the convergence rate of a cubature rule. We study this effect for equal-weight integration on spheres and determine how accurately the nodes must be realized to retain optimal Sobolev rates. Under an average energy condition on the reference nodes, we establish sharp perturbation bounds and characterize how the decay of node errors affects quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) strength, which measures the smoothness range over which optimal rates hold. We identify when this strength is preserved and when it can decrease, and show that sufficiently slow decay of node errors can destroy all optimal Sobolev rates. For a reference rule with optimal convergence, we further establish a necessary and sufficient condition on node accuracy for retaining the optimal rate uniformly over all permitted perturbations. Numerical experiments with spherical designs, Fekete points, and Coulomb-energy points illustrate the different stability regimes.
item.dc:creator: Hao-Ning Wu

item.title: Random Projection Neural Networks for Phase-Field Models: Model Reformulation, Scaling, and Network Architecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.28859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phase-field models, particularly the Allen-Cahn(AC) and Cahn-Hilliard(CH) equations, are widely used to describe interfacial dynamics, but resolving their sharp transition layers and stiff dynamics presents substantial numerical challenges. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) offer a mesh-free approach, yet optimizing large numbers of network parameters can be computationally demanding and may still yield limited accuracy. We develop a random projection neural network (RPNN) framework that combines first-order PDE reformulations with independent random-feature representations of the unknowns. By fixing randomly initialized hidden-layer parameters and optimizing only the output coefficients, RPNNs reduce training to least-squares problems amenable to Newton-type solvers. Introducing auxiliary variables eliminates higher-order derivatives from the PDE residuals, while separate random feature bases in the unknowns provide flexibility in approximating fields with different scales and regularity. For the CH equation, we scale the chemical potential to address the disparity between its magnitude and that of the phase field. We compare the first-order and corresponding higher-order formulations and systematically examine the effects of initialization distributions, the random feature range $R_\xi$, seven activation functions, and dense versus separable space-time bases. We also evaluate gradient-based adaptive sampling, residual reweighting, and mild spatial derivative-penalty regularization. Across the reported benchmarks, the proposed framework reduces relative $L^2$ and absolute $L^\infty$ errors by nearly one to three orders of magnitude compared with the various PINN baselines. These results demonstrate the potential of first-order RPNNs for accurate approximation of phase-field dynamics with sharp transition layers.
item.dc:creator: Chunyan Li, Qi Wang

item.title: Learning the Boltzmann Collision Operator with Structural Constraints for Fast Kinetic Simulation
item.description: arXiv:2611.28864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The high-dimensional integration in the Boltzmann collision operator is a major computational bottleneck in deterministic kinetic simulations. We develop a structure-preserving neural operator that provides an efficient approximation of this nonlinear collision mapping. The operator maintains the gain-loss structure of the original Boltzmann collision operator, and, by construction, is proportional to the square of the gas density. Conservative moment projection and entropy correction enforce conservation of mass, momentum, and energy, as well as entropy dissipation. By construction, the collision term also vanishes at all Maxwellians. In the numerical scheme for simulations of gas dynamics, we establish nonnegativity of the distribution function with the learned collision operator and prove exponential relaxation to the moment-matched equilibrium when a positive spectral gap is imposed. Numerical experiments for a constant collision kernel demonstrate a favorable accuracy-cost tradeoff relative to Fourier spectral evaluations. Although trained on smooth distributions, the same operator handles discontinuous distribution functions and is embedded without retraining in steady Couette flow, normal-shock, and two-dimensional lid-driven cavity solvers. These results demonstrate a reusable approximation for repeated collision evaluations that retains kinetic structure and supports accurate deterministic simulation.
item.dc:creator: Hao Wang, Zhenning Cai

item.title: An Efficient Long-Time Stable Second-Order Ensemble Method for the Parameterized Navier--Stokes Equations
item.description:
arXiv:2611.28896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ensemble simulations for uncertainty quantification, ensemble forecasting, and long-time statistics require stability over arbitrarily long horizons without time-step restrictions. We develop a second-order ensemble method for parameterized incompressible Navier--Stokes equations that uses a common, time-independent Brinkman (shifted Stokes) operator for all members. The scheme combines BDF2, a mean-reverting scalar auxiliary variable (mr-SAV) treatment of convection, and viscosity splitting with a shared viscosity $ ar
u$ treated implicitly and memberwise deviations explicitly. For constant viscosities satisfying $0<
u_j<4 ar
u/3$, we establish unconditional, uniform-in-time dissipativity under uniformly bounded forcing, including an absorbing bound independent of initial data and time-step size. We show that the upper viscosity threshold is sharp for fixed $ ar
u$. For spatially varying random viscosities, unconditional long-time stability holds under a signed pointwise condition that confines $
u_j$ to $( ar
u/3,4 ar
u/3)$ uniformly away from the endpoints; for proportional spatial profiles, it holds over the full range $0<
u_j<4 ar
u/3$. Under the full-range constant-viscosity condition and sufficient regularity in two dimensions, we prove second-order temporal error bounds for velocity, the auxiliary variable, and the discrete time primitive of the pressure error. Numerical tests corroborate long-time stability at large time steps and the sharpness of the viscosity threshold, demonstrate accurate individual solutions and ensemble statistics, and show that mean reversion prevents long-time drift. Reusing the shared operator reduces computing time by about half relative to member-by-member solves.
item.dc:creator: Daozhi Han, Jiaxuan Liu, Xiaoming Wang, Zhoushun Zheng

item.title: A Class of Monotone Quasi-Newtonian Flows Coupled to Nonlinear Equations: Analysis and Finite Element Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2611.28909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze a monotone quasi-Newtonian flow coupled with nonlinear heat and concentration equations. In the model, the viscosity depends on the temperature, the concentration, and the velocity gradient, and the diffusivities depend on the temperature and the concentration. We show the existence of weak solutions without smallness assumptions on the data, and their uniqueness under suitable smallness and regularity assumptions. For the numerical approximation, we consider the Taylor--Hood and mini elements. We prove that the discrete solutions converge, up to a subsequence, to a weak solution, and we derive a quasi-best approximation result and convergence rates. We present numerical experiments in two and three dimensions that illustrate the theory.
item.dc:creator: Gilberto Campa\~na, V\'ictor Vallejo, Jesus Vellojin

item.title: A Principled Framework for PDE-Based Shock Capturing in High-Order Discontinuous Galerkin Methods
item.description: arXiv:2611.28994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: PDE-based artificial viscosity (AV) captures shocks in high-order discontinuous Galerkin (DG) methods by solving an auxiliary PDE for a smooth viscosity field. The behavior of that field is set by how the terms of the AV PDE scale with the element size $h$ and polynomial degree $p$, and by how its coefficients are parametrized. This work derives both choices from analysis and studies the impact these choices have on the implicit steady-state solver. First, an $L^2$-projection analysis shows that the thinnest shock a polynomial space can represent monotonically scales with the resolution length $\bar h = h/p$, and a scaling analysis of the AV PDE gives concrete conditions on its diffusion and source terms for the solution to be self-similar in $\bar h$. Prior formulations satisfy them only under $h$-refinement at fixed $p$; the AV PDE is scaled so that they hold under $hp$-refinement, and the captured shock thins accordingly. Second, a Green's-function analysis of the steady AV PDE gives closed-form expressions for the width and magnitude of the AV. In the standard parametrization the two are coupled: raising the diffusion coefficient widens the AV but lowers its peak. An alternative parametrization of the decay coefficient removes the coupling in the Green's-function response and inverts it in the coupled state-AV problem, so that widening the AV raises its peak instead of lowering it. Third, a parameter study on a Mach 5 viscous flow over a half-cylinder characterizes how the choice of solution variables and the AV PDE's time, width, and magnitude coefficients affect the robustness and cost of the implicit solve. The choice of variables dominates robustness, with entropy variables converging over the largest region of the width-magnitude parameter space. Together, the three contributions make PDE-based AV more predictable to tune and its implicit solve more robust.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Marques, Alireza H. Razavi, Masayuki Yano, Matthew J. Zahr

item.title: The coordinate dependence of numerical rank: charts adapted to level sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.28998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sampling a smooth field on a grid can give an array of high numerical rank even when the field is simple. A Gaussian ridge rotated off the grid axes is the standard example: in coordinates which follow the ridge, the same field has rank one. The rank therefore depends on the chart, that is, on the coordinates in which the field is sampled. We ask which properties of a chart control this rank. For a field which depends on position only through a function $\phi$, a chart whose coordinate lines follow the level sets of $\phi$ gives rank one. Building on this, we show four things. First, mesh quality does not control rank: a chart whose cells have perfect size and shape can still give infinite rank. Second, when a chart follows the level sets of an estimate of $\phi$, the extra rank depends on a single quantity, the defect, which measures how much the true field varies along each coordinate line. Its size matters only logarithmically, its complexity through a count which cannot be improved in general, and when the defect is simple across the level sets the cost stays small. Third, whether the defect is simple can be checked by differentiating the true level function along the flow which builds the chart. Fourth, rank and invertibility fail differently. When the curve behind an offset chart is perturbed, the rank grows slowly, but the chart stops being invertible abruptly, once the offset exceeds the distance at which neighboring normals of the curve first cross. A chart built from the level sets of a field estimate stays invertible when the gradient of the estimate does not vanish on the band and the coordinate lines along each level set do not cross themselves. Pre-registered experiments in two dimensions show how far the bounds are from the observed ranks, and suggest when each kind of chart is preferable; two choices in the last comparison were made after the experiments.
item.dc:creator: Hung Tran, Duc P. Truong

item.title: On the performance of the randomized Euler scheme for nonlinear ODEs under inexact information
item.description: arXiv:2611.29048v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the randomized explicit Euler scheme for nonlinear ordinary differential equations under a local one-sided Lipschitz condition, local H\"older regularity in the space variable, and H\"older regularity in the time variable. We allow for noisy evaluations of the right-hand side. For the resulting approximation, we derive an error bound in which the contribution associated with the H\"older regularity in the time variable exhibits the characteristic 1/2-order gain of randomized methods. While existing results cover deterministic schemes under the one-sided Lipschitz condition and randomized schemes under the classical Lipschitz condition, our results combine randomized approximation and one-sided Lipschitz regularity.
item.dc:creator: Tomasz Bochacik, Bartosz Fober, Pawe{\l} Przyby{\l}owicz

item.title: On rescuing diverging algorithms: crossing infinity in continuous Newton methods via a self-similarity detection framework
item.description: arXiv:2611.29088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We address the solution of systems of nonlinear algebraic equations via continuous Newton methods; these methods reformulate the discrete Newton update as an initial value problem for a system of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) whose stationary points correspond to the desired roots. A fundamental challenge arises when the Jacobian of these ODEs becomes singular along the solution trajectory, inducing blow-up in the vector field --or in the state itself-- and causing the numerical integration to break down before reaching the desired root. To overcome this difficulty, we propose a directional self-similar blow-up detection and crossing procedure, wrapped around an adaptive step-size ODE solver with event detection. The method assumes local self-similar behavior near the blow-up; the self-similarity exponent, blow-up time, and amplitude are estimated on the fly from a short sequence of threshold crossings via linear regression, requiring no prior knowledge of the singularity location, its order, or the blow-up regime---in contrast to approaches that rely on explicit analytical continuation or problem-specific coordinate transformations. The estimated exponent distinguishes two qualitatively different scenarios at finite time: one in which only the vector field diverges while the state remains finite, admitting an explicit integral correction, and one in which the state itself blows-up. In addition, infinite-time divergence of the state (the so-called "grow-up" regime) is handled through a suitable time reparameterization. In higher dimensions, we track the norm of the vector field along its instantaneous direction; near a simple singularity, the flow asymptotically aligns with a single dominant direction (see text), reducing detection and estimation to a scalar problem regardless of ambient space dimension.
item.dc:creator: Gianluca Fabiani, Ralf Hannemann-Tam\'as, Alexander Mitsos, Jonathan D. Hauenstein, Constantinos Siettos, Panayotis G. Kevrekidis, Ioannis G. Kevrekidis

item.title: Structure-Preserving Analysis of a Nonlinear Reaction--Diffusion Model for Homogeneous Redox Catalysis
item.description: arXiv:2611.29144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a reduced nonlinear reaction--diffusion model for homogeneous redox catalysis under a low-scan-rate, frozen-potential approximation motivated by cyclic voltammetry. The reduced system contains two concentration fields coupled through the same nonlinear reaction term and therefore satisfies, exactly within the reduced model, \[ (a-q)_\tau=(a-q)_{yy}. \] This identity yields an exact reconstruction of the substrate concentration from the electroactive concentration and provides the organizing principle for the structure-preserving approximations developed below. Formulation I applies the homotopy perturbation method (HPM) to the catalyst field using a constant-coefficient Green-function hierarchy and reconstructs the substrate field from the exact heat equation. Formulation II linearizes the nonlinear reaction about a space- and time-dependent reference profile while preserving the same difference structure and the physical far-field state. The methods are evaluated using fourth-order method-of-lines discretizations, direct Green/heat-kernel formulas for the electrode current, and an independently refined nonlinear PDE benchmark. For the baseline problem, the published substrate approximation has maximum error \(1.69\times10^{-1}\), whereas the \(N=3\) errors are reduced to \(2.09\times10^{-5}\) for Formulation I and \(3.61\times10^{-6}\) for Formulation II. At \(N=1\), Formulation II improves the errors in the catalyst, substrate, and current by factors of approximately \(18.2\), \(46.9\), and \(42.1\), respectively, relative to Formulation I. The results show that preserving the exact coupled structure substantially improves accuracy and yields an efficient low-order analytical framework for nonlinear electrochemical reaction--diffusion problems.
item.dc:creator: Guangming Yao, Michael Shaw, Nazia Nimmy, Adriana Silva

item.title: Product Enrichment of Spline Spaces for IGA: Polynomial Reproduction, Approximation, and Stable Computation
item.description: arXiv:2611.29170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study product enrichment of spline spaces under a fixed isoparametric geometry map for isogeometric analysis (IGA). For each fixed integer $\ell\ge1$, a locally $L^\infty$-stable initial operator reproducing $\mathbb P_k$ yields an explicit linear map from $L^2(D)$ into $W_h^\ell$ that reproduces $\mathbb P_{\ell k}$ and is locally stable in $L^2$ and $L^\infty$, uniformly in the mesh scale. Under additional initial-space regularity and derivative stability, the construction gives integer-order Sobolev error estimates of order $h^{s-m}$ for $1\le s\le\ell k+1$ and admissible $m$. Independently, the geometry representation implies reproduction of physical polynomials of degree at most $\ell$ by the enriched space. Polynomial containment also yields algebraic and analytic best-approximation estimates as the product order increases. For every fixed product order, we give a compatible redundant Galerkin formulation and an explicit initial-space injection. A local spectral construction and an initial-space correction give a two-level energy condition-number bound without requiring independent product generators. These solver results concern exact arithmetic; coarse-space cost, quadrature consistency, boundary constraints, and numerical rank truncation require separate control.
item.dc:creator: Shaojie Luo, Yuanpeng Zhu

item.title: A Hyper-Reduced Reduced Order Model Built From Streaming Tensor Train Data
item.description: arXiv:2611.29190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low-rank PDE solvers based on tensor-decompositions inside physical space leverages low-rank structures across different physical dimensions, while projection-based reduced order models (ROMs) for parametric PDEs exploit low-rank structures across parameter spaces. Recently, to use the complimentary strength of these two methods, a ROM framework is proposed by incrementally constructing compressed reduced bases directly from streaming tensor-train (TT) snapshots provided by low-rank solvers, but it omits hyper reduction and consequently incur substantial online costs for nonlinear or non-affine parametric PDEs. To address this issue, we develop a hyper-reduced TT ROM for streaming TT data by combining incremental low-rank TT compression and nested TT discrete empirical interpolation (TT-DEIM). Numerical experiments on nonlinear and non-affine parametric PDEs achieve mean relative errors, matching the accuracy of non-hyper-reduced TT-Galerkin ROMs while achieving mean online speedups of approximately 8 times to 1500 times compared to them.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoshan Wu, Zhichao Peng

item.title: Ordering error estimates under mesh-uniform regularity and optimal two-mesh design for the KdV equation with boundary dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2611.29196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Galerkin error estimates and optimal two-mesh design for the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation. The ordering error is introduced to measure how much the nonlinearity changes the discretization error. A weighted cubic Hermite Galerkin scheme has mesh-uniform regularity: the discrete semigroups of the linearized equation inherit Crandall-Pazy regularity and Kato smoothing, with bounds uniform in the mesh size $h$. On a small ball of the energy space, the discrete solution maps are also analytic in the initial datum, with bounds uniform in $h$. On this ball the ordering error is at most of order $h^{1/6}$ times the squared energy norm of the datum, for all $t\ge0$. For $u_0$ on this ball and in the domain $D(A)$ of the linearized generator, the bound is of order $h^2\|u_0\|_{H^3}^{3/2}\|u_0\|_{L^2}^{1/2}$. A two-mesh computation adds a nonlinear correction on a coarse mesh to a linear simulation on a fine mesh. Its error is the linear error on the fine mesh plus the ordering error on the coarse mesh. Based on these error estimates, we formulate a model of the optimal two-mesh design: minimize the cost subject to an accuracy constraint given by the error bounds. For data in a small ball of $L^2$, the problem is convex in logarithmic mesh sizes. When the relative error bound for the coarsest allowed mesh exceeds the prescribed tolerance $\eta$, the optimal pair and its KKT multipliers are unique. For smooth data the problem is convex in the mesh sizes, and the optimal mesh ratio is independent of the tolerance until the coarse mesh reaches its upper limit. In both cases we characterize the small-amplitude limit of the relative cost when the relative tolerance is proportional to the amplitude.
item.dc:creator: Kangsheng Liu

item.title: Efficient numerical computation of the generalized Marcum $Q$-function with applications
item.description:
arXiv:2611.29209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The computation of the generalized Marcum $Q$-function, $Q_
u(a,b)$, is fundamental to radar detection and wireless communications. The state-of-the-art 	extbf{Algorithm 939} (Gil et al., ACM TOMS 2014) serves as the current gold standard by employing a hybrid evaluation scheme combining series expansions, asymptotic formulas, numerical integration and recurrence relations. However, it suffers from a computational bottleneck: in the ``large $a$, small $b$'' regime, the algorithm resorts to computationally expensive numerical quadrature, thereby limiting its overall efficiency. To bridge this gap, we utilize a series representation of the generalized Marcum $Q$-function to construct the Series Expansion based on Recurrence Relations (	extbf{SE-RR}) algorithm. Expanded in powers of $b$, this series computes its coefficients via a stable recurrence relation, resulting in a remarkably low computational cost. By analyzing rounding, truncation and cancellation errors, we identify the optimal region for SE-RR as the ``large $a$, small $b$'' regime, which covers the parameter space where Algorithm~939 relies on costly numerical quadrature. Consequently, we integrate SE-RR into Algorithm~939 to develop a hybrid algorithm for evaluating $Q_
u(a,b)$. Benchmarked against $10^7$ log-uniformly sampled parameter triples $(a, b, 
u) \in [0.01, 100] 	imes [0.001, 100] 	imes [1, 1000]$, the hybrid algorithm achieves an average speedup of 82.2\% overall, while in the region where SE-RR is applied, it delivers an average speedup of 156.6\% and a maximum pointwise speedup of $\mathrm{5.49}	imes$. Finally, we demonstrate the practical utility of the hybrid algorithm by computing the cumulative distribution function of the noncentral chi distribution and outage probabilities for 5G/6G ultra-reliable low-latency communications.
item.dc:creator: Zhong-Xuan Mao, Jing-Feng Tian

item.title: Verified parameter estimation for differential-equation models: NIST reference problems and the theophylline flip-flop
item.description: arXiv:2611.29216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parameters fitted to differential-equation models carry two kinds of error: statistical error from noisy data, and numerical error from the solver and the optimizer that compute the fit. Standard fitting tools report the first and leave the second unexamined, and they return one optimum without saying whether another parameter set fits the data equally well. We describe SIRPY, a differential-equation solver that checks every solution it returns by substituting it back into the equation, and we test it in two settings. First, on eleven nonlinear-regression reference problems from the US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), each written as a first-order differential equation and fitted by least squares with every model curve supplied by SIRPY, the estimates agree with NIST's certified values to 7.1 to 8.8 significant digits on ten problems, with all 6{,}281 solves verified; the eleventh problem exposed a limitation of the residual check, which we report and explain. Second, on the classic theophylline pharmacokinetic data, SIRPY found two parameter sets whose predicted curves agree to within $1.7\times10^{-11}$~mg/L and matched the reference fit from the R package \texttt{nlme} to every printed digit; the data alone cannot decide which rate is absorption and which is elimination, and physiology must. We state precisely what the verification certifies, what it does not, and what remains to be done to turn a residual check into a proven bound on estimation error.
item.dc:creator: Hamid Semiyari

item.title: A Parallel APSOR SPIKE Algorithm for Classical and Soft Layer Obstacle Problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.29220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a parallel scheme for classical obstacle problems and for obstacle problems with a soft layer. The adaptive projected SOR method (APSOR) \cite{MS21} finds the contact set on one process. The linear system defined by the frozen contact set is then solved exactly in parallel by the SPIKE algorithm \cite{PS06}, in which the diagonal blocks are factorized independently and the coupling is condensed into a small reduced system. The remaining nonlinearity of the soft-layer problem \cite{CRWX21} is resolved by a Picard iteration in which every pass reuses the factorization, and a Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) test stops the iteration. The scheme needs no tuned relaxation parameter. Convergence is proved: APSOR decreases the energy, the SPIKE solve is exact and independent of the number of processes, the Picard iteration is a contraction with factor below $0.052$ on the unit square, and under strict complementarity the loop stops at the unique KKT point. Four classical problems \cite{TSFO14} and four soft-layer examples \cite{CRWX21} in one and two dimensions are computed and compared with exact and analytic solutions (maximum errors $1.1\times10^{-8}$, $7.2\times10^{-14}$ and $6.0\times10^{-4}$), and the KKT test is passed in all eight runs. CPU timings with 1 to 16 MPI ranks show that the SPIKE decomposition takes most of the time in two dimensions, so that the part that is distributed over the ranks is the dominant part of the work.
item.dc:creator: Amboru Yalamanda, Peeyush Singh

item.title: Mass- and energy-preserving low-regularity integrators for nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.29326v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation is a fundamental model of dispersive wave phenomena, possessing a rich geometric structure that includes the conservation of mass and energy. Preserving these conservation laws at the level of numerical discretisation remains challenging, particularly for solutions of low regularity. In particular, combining the favourable convergence properties of low-regularity integrators with the exact preservation of fundamental conservation laws has remained an open challenge. In this work, we introduce, to the best of our knowledge, the first mass- and energy-preserving low-regularity integrators for the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation. We establish the well-posedness and convergence of the proposed schemes and demonstrate how ideas from projection methods can be used to ensure the simultaneous preservation of mass and energy. Our rigorous analysis (the first for mass- and energy-preserving schemes) is supported by extensive numerical experiments highlighting the favourable convergence and structure-preserving properties of the methods, including for rough solutions.
item.dc:creator: Tianyu Jin, Georg Maierhofer

item.title: On mesh transfers and time error estimation in adaptive finite element methods for parabolic problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.29379v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In space and time adaptive finite element methods, the discrete solution is transferred onto a different mesh whenever the spatial mesh changes. Refinement is commonly regarded as harmless, since nodal interpolation then reproduces the discrete solution exactly. However, we show that for the implicit Euler method applied to the heat equation, the transferred solution and time derivative, in general, violate the discrete equation on the new mesh. Unless the resulting transfer residual vanishes, the corresponding time error estimator overestimates the local error, for small time steps, by a factor inversely proportional to the time step size. To address this issue, we propose transfers based on the elliptic reconstruction, which significantly reduce the transfer residual or even remove it. In numerical experiments, we confirm the analysis and demonstrate the advantages of the proposed transfers in a space and time adaptive example.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Karch

item.title: Convergence of Nonmonotone Schemes to Viscosity Solutions via Local Comparison
item.description: arXiv:2611.29522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a convergence criterion for nonmonotone approximation schemes for Hamilton--Jacobi and fully nonlinear second-order equations. Under stability, consistency and suitable boundary assumptions, a local comparison hypothesis replaces monotonicity and yields convergence to viscosity solutions. For a semi-Lagrangian CWENO scheme for one-dimensional Hamilton--Jacobi equations, we establish convergence for bounded uniformly continuous initial data under $h=o(\tau)$, relaxing the previously required mesh condition $h=O(\tau^2)$. We also prove convergence of a nonmonotone one-dimensional $Q^2$ scheme for Isaacs equations whose operator cannot be written as a monotone operator plus a perturbation vanishing uniformly on bounded grid functions.
item.dc:creator: Alessio Basti, Fabio Camilli

item.title: Model order reduction for space-time DPG approximations of the Schr\"odinger equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.29685v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work extends the ultraweak space-time discontinuous Petrov-Galerkin (DPG) method for the linear time-dependent Schr\"odinger equation, introduced in [Demkowicz, Gopalakrishnan et al., SINUM 2017], from the free equation to bounded, time-independent, real-valued potentials. Continuous well-posedness is established in the graph norms with a potential-independent inf-sup constant. The potential is parametrized and the discretization is combined with model order reduction. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this is the first explicit coupling of the DPG methodology with reduced basis methods. Uniform well-posedness with respect to parameter-independent reference norms is proven and yields exponential decay of the Kolmogorov $N$-widths. Moreover, the distinctive structural features of this combination are discussed, in particular the parameter dependence of the optimal test spaces and norms, and the built-in residual-based error control of the DPG framework, which drives a greedy reduced basis construction. Numerical experiments in one spatial dimension for both parameter-independent and parametrized potentials support the theoretical results and demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the resulting reduced-order models.
item.dc:creator: Timo Keith, Mario Ohlberger

item.title: Accurate rank-controlled step-truncation methods for matrix differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.29710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A class of explicit time stepping schemes is introduced for the integration of matrix differential equations in low-rank format. These schemes combine explicit Runge-Kutta time stepping with rank-adaptive recompressions. For suitably chosen truncation thresholds, they converge at arbitrary order, while having close to optimal ranks, without any prior assumptions on the best approximation ranks. The ranks of the scheme also necessarily depend on the time step, as shown by counterexamples. A numerical experiment illustrates the advantages and performance of the proposed scheme.
item.dc:creator: Matthieu Dolbeault, Polina Sachsenmaier, Fabio Zoccolan

item.title: Essentially Order-Preserving Fourth-Order Exponential Runge--Kutta Methods for Non-Commuting Operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.29826v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the convergence of explicit exponential Runge--Kutta methods for the linear evolution equation \(u'(t)+Au(t)=Bu(t)\), where \(-A\) generates an analytic semigroup, \(B\) is unbounded and relatively bounded with respect to \(A\), and \(A\) and \(B\) do not commute. It is known from our previous work on order reduction of exponential Runge--Kutta methods for non-commuting operators that this non-commutativity can cause order reduction even for linear problems. In a further work on third-order methods, we showed that this reduction can be avoided by adding a stage and imposing higher regularity on the initial data. Here we treat the fourth-order case. We identify conditions on the coefficients of explicit fourth-order exponential Runge--Kutta methods under which the full order four is retained for this class of problems, and we state the convergence rate as a function of the regularity of \(u_0\). The analysis shows precisely which defect terms, caused by the non-commutativity of \(A\) and \(B\), are eliminated by these conditions. The classical methods of Krogstad and of Strehmel--Weiner do not satisfy them and converge only with order \(11/4\) under the corresponding regularity assumptions, whereas the six-stage method expRK4s6, constructed by Luan (2021), satisfies them and attains order four. Numerical experiments for an advection--diffusion problem involving non-commuting operators confirm the theoretical convergence rates.
item.dc:creator: Thi Tam Dang, Trung Hau Hoang

item.title: Schur decomposition with logarithmic precision in cubic time up to logarithmic factors
item.description: arXiv:2611.29923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How much arithmetic precision is needed to compute a Schur decomposition to a prescribed tolerance? Let $A$ be a complex matrix of order $n$ with spectral norm at most one, let $0<\delta<1/2$ be the tolerance, and let $0<p<1/2$ be the requested failure probability. Our randomised floating-point algorithm uses $O(\log(n/(\delta p)))$ mantissa bits per real component and $O(n^3\log^2(n/(\delta p)))$ arithmetic operations on every execution, with universal constants. It returns $Q$ and an exactly upper triangular $T$. With probability at least $1-p$, both $\|A-QTQ^*\|_2$ and $\|Q^*Q-I\|_2$ are at most $\delta$. We sample a small perturbation using finitely many bits and use Gaussian estimates to bound the eigenvector conditioning and eigenvalue gap. A single contour estimate bounds the effect of a rounding error through any number of remaining Newton steps. At each subdivision level, the full matrix is unitarily similar to a small perturbation of the regularised input. This allows us to bound the conditioning of each diagonal block directly from that input and to use the same precision throughout.
item.dc:creator: Matthew J. Colbrook

item.title: Stabilized Isogeometric Topology Optimization on Trimmed Geometries
item.description: arXiv:2611.29940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a novel stabilized isogeometric topology optimization method for complex design domains represented by trimmed geometries. Minimum compliance is taken as the model problem, where a generalized Cahn-Hilliard model, a time-dependent fourth-order partial differential equation, is solved and its steady-state solutions yield the optimized structures. This approach does not require sensitivity analysis and can naturally accommodate material constraints and complex topological changes. To impose Dirichlet boundary conditions and solve the instability issue caused by trimming, Nitsche's formulation with minimal stabilization is proposed for the high-order problem. Moreover, the immersed boundary-conformal method is extended to handle complex non-design domains, allowing material-void interfaces to be treated in a unified manner. Finally, a three-dimensional biharmonic problem and several two-dimensional topology optimization examples are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness, stability, and flexibility of the proposed method in dealing with complex design domains.
item.dc:creator: Haoyu Su, Giuliano Guarino, Xiaodong Wei

item.title: Hierarchical randomized neural networks for efficiently and accurately finding multiple solutions of semilinear elliptic equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.30010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Being able to find multiple solutions of a semilinear elliptic equation is a fundamental problem in scientific computing. In this paper, fully taking the advantages of randomized neural networks, we propose a new efficient and accurate method for identifying potentially as many solutions as possible. The new method is constructed from three aspects--initialization, optimization, a technique for acceleration and improving accuracy, two of which are innovative developments. Firstly, based on the basis functions of a randomized network and the sampling points, a characteristic matrix is introduced so that its singular value decomposition can be used to determine weakly variant search directions, followed by a newly developed algorithm to generate effective initial candidates. Then the good deflated Gauss-Newton method [see {\em A. Riley, et al., SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 47~(5) (2025) A2963-A2987}] using an exponential deflation operator is adapted as the optimization to search for all multiple solutions. Local error estimate of a particular solution under some proper condition is given in terms of the neurons in the hidden layer and the sampling points for this newly designed method. Furthermore, to accelerate the computation and improve the solution accuracy, a new multilevel method based on hierarchical networks is designed. Without using any {\em a priori} information, several numerical tests show together with the multilevel method, the new method can not only accurately find multiple solutions with relative errors reaching $10^{-16}$ only in less than one-tenth computational cost for the best case, but also preserve the inherent symmetries of multiple solutions.
item.dc:creator: Jingying Hu, Jiao Li, Yufeng Xu, Jinyong Ying

item.title: A High-Order Geometry-Conforming Selective Discontinuous Galerkin Method and Its Error Analysis for Elliptic Interface Problems on Curved Domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.30169v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop and analyze a high-order geometry-conforming immersed finite element (GC-IFE) method for elliptic interface problems on curved domains. The method uses a triangular mesh that conforms to the outer boundary but need not fit the internal interface. Using Frenet--Serret coordinates, the method combines GC-IFE spaces on interface elements, geometry-conforming finite element spaces on curved boundary elements, and standard Lagrange spaces elsewhere. The global degrees of freedom of the proposed method are asymptotically the same as that of the standard continuous finite element method on the same mesh. The main analytical contributions are approximation estimates and trace inequalities for triangular GC-IFE functions. These estimates are used to establish stability and an optimal $O(h^m)$ error bound in an energy norm for the proposed method, which is based on a symmetric selective discontinuous Galerkin formulation. An optimal $O(h^{m+1})$ error bound in the $L^2$ norm is also obtained under the standard regularity assumption on the dual problem. Numerical experiments confirm theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate a reduction in global degrees of freedom to a fully discontinuous Galerkin method.
item.dc:creator: Fang Liu, Yuanhui Liu, Tao Lin, Xu Zhang

item.title: Numerical simulations of CCP-2D GEC with sGMRES
item.description: arXiv:2611.30211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fluid models provide an efficient means of simulating the low-temperature gas discharges, which are important in semiconductor manufacturing. This work presents, to the best of our knowledge, the first systematic numerical framework for the Gaseous Electronics Conference (GEC) reference cell of the 2D capacitively coupled plasma (CCP). The framework employs a structured, nonuniform cylindrical mesh to resolve the spatial gradients. A semi-implicit Scharfetter-Gummel (SG) scheme is used for the Poisson's equation, while the implicit SG schemes are applied to the continuity equations and the electron energy equation. Both the explicit and and the implicit formulations based on the conventional drift-diffusion terms are also investigated. To solve the resulting large-scale linear systems, we introduce an incomplete LU (ILU)-preconditioned sketched GMRES (sGMRES) method as the solver. As far as we know, this work is the first to apply the randomized sGMRES to the practical simulations in the engineering. By reducing the cost of the global orthogonalization, ILU-sGMRES achieves greater computational efficiency than ILU-GMRES while maintaining the accuracy, particularly at relatively large values of the restart. Specifically, numerical tests demonstrate that ILU-sGMRES can reduce the end-to-end wall-clock time by up to 25.38\% on a single machine and up to 11.71\% in a three-node benchmark compared with the conventional ILU-GMRES, while maintaining a maximum relative difference across plasma fields of only 0.194\%. Numerical experiments compare the performance of different numerical schemes and solvers, demonstrating the robustness of ILU-sGMRES in the real simulation.
item.dc:creator: Zhenyu Zou, Haoran Guan, Kangxin Liu, Yufeng Wei, Yipei Chen, Peiting You, Yuwei Fan

item.title: Backward Error and Scaling in Level-Based ILU(k) and IC(k) Preconditioners
item.description: arXiv:2611.30282v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyse the effect of rounding errors and diagonal scaling on level-based ILU($k$) and IC($k$) preconditioners. Because the sparsity pattern is fixed in advance, the computed factors are those that the incomplete factorization produces, in exact arithmetic, for a nearby matrix, and the deviation of the preconditioned matrix from the identity is bounded by an incompleteness term plus a rounding term. When no shift or pivot modification is needed, scaling leaves the iterates unchanged in exact arithmetic but can change the quantities in this bound by orders of magnitude. For IC($k$), we bound the change in the preconditioned eigenvalues caused by rounding by a multiple of the Skeel condition number of the incomplete factor, which does not depend on the scaling, and we show that after Jacobi scaling the entries of the factor are bounded, so that in half precision a breakdown can be detected before any overflow. Experiments in double, single and half precision illustrate the theory.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Scott, Miroslav T\r{u}ma

item.title: A preconditioned Reconstructed Discontinuous Approximation for Darcy flow
item.description: arXiv:2611.30355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop an efficient numerical method for Darcy flow based on the reconstructed discontinuous approximation (RDA). The key contribution is a mesh-robust piecewise-constant preconditioner for arbitrarily high-order RDA discretizations of Darcy flow. The method discretizes the Darcy equations by a stabilized discontinuous Galerkin scheme in coupled velocity-pressure form, with RDA spaces for both velocity and pressure. Function spaces of this type can achieve arbitrarily high-order approximation accuracy while retaining only one degree of freedom per element. We establish an optimal-order error estimate in the energy norm and a suboptimal error estimate in the L2 norm. Benefiting from the property that the number of degrees of freedom of the RDA space is independent of the approximation order, we can construct a simple and efficient preconditioner based on piecewise constant functions for algebraic systems arising from arbitrarily high-order discretizations. We further prove a mesh-independent spectral equivalence between the preconditioner and the original algebraic system, so that the convergence of the GMRES residual does not slow down under mesh refinement. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions confirm the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed preconditioning method.
item.dc:creator: Ming Cui, Yanxiang Gao, Ruo Li, Qicheng Liu, Fanyi Yang, Shuhai Zhao

item.title: New applications for optimal adaptivity
item.description: arXiv:2611.30398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce an explicit time-stepping scheme for ODEs, together with a residual-based a posteriori error estimator. Using this estimator, we show a new approach to proving optimality and linear reduction of adaptive algorithms for time-dependent problems that works in $H^1(0, t_{\rm end})$ and $W^{1,\infty}(0,t_{\rm end})$ norms, does not require quasi-orthogonality, and poses no restrictions on the marking parameter $\theta$. The key idea is to use the Lipschitz continuity of the semi-discretized operator to obtain a stronger form of estimator reduction. Numerical experiments illustrate the benefits of this explicit scheme coupled with adaptive refinement over uniform time stepping for classical evolution problems, regularized dynamical approximation, and neural ODEs.
item.dc:creator: Michael Feischl, J\"org Nick, David Niederkofler

item.title: Newton iterations and semi-Lagrangian schemes for mean field games of controls
item.description: arXiv:2611.30409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Newton methods for second-order mean field games of controls (MFGC), in which agents interact through local averages of their controls. We prove local quadratic convergence of full Newton iterations, and of Newton iterations on reduced unknowns, near stable classical solutions. Stability holds under weak control interaction and under an infinitesimal monotonicity condition of Lasry--Lions type. We propose a semi-Lagrangian (SL) scheme for second-order MFGC, in which the average-control relation is solved by a convergent Chebyshev iteration, and two matrix-free solvers: a full Newton--SL method with block Gauss--Seidel preconditioning, whose spectrum we characterize in the absence of control coupling, and a reduced Jacobian-free Newton--GMRES method whose density iterates are nonnegative and mass-preserving by construction. We also construct an exact, time-dependent, coupled MFGC solution for use as a benchmark. In the experiments, the reduced solver converges quadratically in its final iterations, also in a strong-alignment test in which full Newton updates lose positivity. On the benchmark, the SL scheme and a finite-difference scheme both converge at first order with errors of comparable size, and our SL implementation is faster.
item.dc:creator: Ahmad Zorkot

item.title: One-shot identification of analytic systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.30470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study when the coefficients of a linearly parameterized analytic system can be identified from a single input-solution pair. Given a finite dictionary of analytic operators, each admissible input induces a finite-dimensional linear recovery map from coefficients to observed outputs. Coefficient recovery is possible exactly when this map is injective. We define the degenerate input set as the set of inputs for which injectivity fails and prove a zero-one law: either every admissible input is degenerate, or the degenerate set is negligible in the sense that it is compactly slice-null and has zero measure under every nondegenerate Gaussian measure. We then apply this framework to the recovery of matrices, analytic continuous-time dynamical systems, and differential operators. For several ODE and PDE classes, we further characterize the degenerate sets explicitly and identify deterministic choices of inputs that guarantee recovery.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Boull\'e, Diana Halikias, Samuel E. Otto, Alex Townsend

item.title: A new frequency-time hybrid RPML-BIE solver with few-mode corrections for the wave-equation problems in nonuniform closed waveguides
item.description: arXiv:2611.30579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is devoted to proposing a novel FTH integral equation solver for wave-equation problems in two-dimensional nonuniform closed waveguides with multiple channels. The FTH methodology, which combines the Fourier transform with frequency-domain BIE formulations, has demonstrated its effectiveness in solving time-dependent wave scattering problems. However, when applied to waveguide problems, the modal expansions arising from multiple scattering introduce cut-off frequencies. Such frequencies pose significant challenges, requiring both a frequency-robust solver for frequency-domain waveguide problems and an efficient treatment of the solution's non-smooth behavior near the cut-off frequencies for the evaluation of the inverse Fourier transform. The first issue is addressed by developing a new frequency-domain BIE method based on the free-space fundamental solution and regionalized perfectly matched layer truncation, together with a few-mode Dirichlet-to-Robin modification. The method is rigorously proved to achieve uniform exponential convergence, even at frequencies arbitrarily close to the cut-off frequencies. To address the second issue---the recovery of the time-domain solution via the inverse Fourier transform---a sine-transform based stationary-point Filon--Clenshaw--Curtis quadrature is introduced to accurately handle the non-smoothness and square-root singularities of frequency-domain solutions. Additionally, theoretical result shows that the complex resonances closing to the real axis may significantly effect the convergence of the Fourier transform algorithm and then a novel strategy of complex resonance extraction based on AAA rational approximation and singularity subtraction is utilized to avoid this influence. Numerical experiments for both frequency-domain and time-domain problems illustrate the efficiency and high accuracy of the proposed method.
item.dc:creator: Yan Tan, Liwei Xu, Tao Yin

item.title: Revisiting the role of reorthogonalisation in LSQR
item.description: arXiv:2611.30626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we revisit the role of reorthogonalisation in the LSQR method for large-scale overdetermined linear least-squares problems. Motivated primarily by practical applications where matrix--vector products dominate the computational cost and only a limited number of iterations can be afforded because of time and/or memory restrictions, we investigate when reorthogonalisation can significantly accelerate convergence. Through synthetic test problems with controlled singular value distributions and experiments on practical sparse problems, we demonstrate that reorthogonalisation is particularly beneficial when the least-squares matrix has large outlying singular values. In such cases, loss of orthogonality can severely delay convergence. We explore the effectiveness of full (one-sided) reorthogonalisation when using LSQR, and present alternative reorthogonalisation strategies that can provide substantial acceleration compared to no reorthogonalisation and significant storage savings compared to full reorthogonalisation. The possibility of using low precision arithmetic for the reorthogonalisation is also investigated. We present bounds that demonstrate the quality of the solution depends on the level of orthogonality maintained by the selected reorthogonalisation strategy. Our results suggest that reorthogonalisation should be regarded as a practical tool for modern least-squares applications that can be employed instead of, or in addition to, preconditioning.
item.dc:creator: Ieva Dau\v{z}ickait\.e, Melina A. Freitag, Selime G\"urol, Amos S. Lawless, Alison Ramage, Jennifer A. Scott, Jemima M. Tabeart

item.title: Certified Finite Element Error Bounds for Diffusion Equations with Measure-Valued Principal-Part Delays
item.description: arXiv:2611.30709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive computable a posteriori finite element error bounds for diffusion equations whose highest-order spatial operator carries a non-negative measure-valued delay. Although the delay law is replaced by finitely many atoms in computations, the bounds measure the error with respect to the solution for the original law. An equilibrated Raviart--Thomas flux controls the spatial residual, and a transport estimate on the computed time reconstruction controls the delay-law residual without additional temporal regularity of the exact solution. A cumulative-mass representation preserves cancellation in this residual and allows a jump between the numerical initial state and the prescribed history. The constants are independent of the mesh aspect ratios and of the number of atoms, and inexact flux equilibration and errors in the elementwise residual means are included. We also give a quantile-based budget for the delay residual and a weighted finite-horizon bound beyond the mass-subcritical regime. Under an elliptic equilibration hypothesis, we prove a two-sided estimate for a combined error norm that includes the time derivative. On right-triangular meshes satisfying the maximum-angle condition, however, the lowest-order Raviart--Thomas estimator can exceed the combined graph error by a factor at least proportional to the aspect ratio. Numerical experiments on anisotropic meshes, including a law beyond the mass-subcritical regime, illustrate the behaviour of the residual indicators and the limitations of efficiency.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Ishizaka

item.title: A particle method for the space homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.30808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a structure preserving particle method to numerically approximate the spatially homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation for collisional plasmas. The Lenard-Balescu operator is an improvement of the Landau equation with a dielectric function taking the dynamic screening effect into account. Our particle method is based on the variational formulation of the Lenard-Balescu equation under suitable regularization analogous to the strategy followed for the Landau collision operator in [12]. The method guarantees the conservation laws and the entropy dissipation at the semi-discrete level. The novel difficulty of the nonlocal nonlinear dependence of the dielectric function is tackled by rewriting it as integrals in terms of orthogonal and parallel components to the frequency variable. This equivalent form reduces the evaluation of the dielectric function to numerically computing an integral of the directional derivative of the solution on a hyperplane orthogonal to the frequency variable and its one-dimensional Hilbert transform. An efficient implementation of the numerical approximation for the Lenard-Balescu kernel is derived by exploiting this expression of the dielectric function. We finally validate our method by means of several numerical tests, further allowing us to explore qualitative properties of the Lenard-Balescu equation.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Antonio Carrillo, Timon Gutleb, Andrea Medaglia, Yijia Tang

item.title: A geometric-IEQ approach for curvature-driven flows
item.description: arXiv:2611.30832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a geometric invariant energy quadratization (IEQ) formulation for the $L^2$-gradient flow of a class of curvature-dependent energies of closed hypersurfaces, where the energy density depends on the mean curvature and the unit normal. A square-root auxiliary variable converts the geometric energy into a quadratic functional. Combining its evolution equation with a skew-symmetric treatment of surface transport yields a weak formulation whose energy law depends only on the normal velocity and is therefore independent of the chosen tangential motion. We construct monolithic nonlinear parametric finite element methods by coupling a common IEQ discretization with one of two geometric formulations that accommodate either the Barrett-Garcke-N\"urnberg (BGN) tangential velocity or the minimal-deformation-rate (MDR) tangential velocity. Both fully discrete approximations satisfy an unconditional decay estimate for the discrete quadratic energy. We further extend the construction to anisotropic Willmore flow, and to $H^{-1}$-gradient flows. A variety of numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the robustness and accuracy of the introduced methods.
item.dc:creator: Harald Garcke, Yifei Li, Robert N\"urnberg, Quan Zhao

item.title: A Hitchhiker's Guide to LR B-Splines
item.description: arXiv:2611.30942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We review the theoretical foundations of locally refined (LR) B-splines, a natural extension of univariate B-splines to multivariate, locally refined, and generally unstructured box partitions. LR B-splines are defined using standard tools from B-spline theory, such as knot insertion, and retain key properties including locality, non-negativity, and a piecewise polynomial structure. Our presentation starts from the definition of spline spaces over box partitions and discusses the instability of their dimension formula due to the presence of a homological term. Conditions ensuring the stabilization of the dimension naturally motivate the construction of LR meshes and LR B-splines. We subsequently analyze the spanning properties of LR B-splines, with particular emphasis on completeness, linear dependence, and local linear independence. We also address known characterizations and refinement strategies ensuring that the resulting LR B-splines preserve the desirable properties of tensor-product B-splines.
item.dc:creator: Carla Manni, Francesco Patrizi, Hendrik Speleers

item.title: A discontinuous Galerkin method for the evolutionary Navier-Stokes-Darcy model
item.description: arXiv:2611.30943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we have analysed a discontinuous Galerkin (DG) method for the coupled surface-subsurface flow, which is modelled by the evolutionary Navier-Stokes-Darcy (NSD) equations. While the DG method has been applied for the spatial discretization of both Navier-Stokes and Darcy equations, for time, we have employed the first-order backward Euler scheme. The fully discrete error analysis has been carried out for both velocity and pressure of the Navier-Stokes equations, and for the piezometric head of the Darcy equation, and optimal estimates have been derived. Our analysis relies on appropriate treatments of the nonlinear convective term from the Navier-Stokes equations, along with the interface conditions that couple the system. We have employed a modified Oseen operator on an appropriate DG setup along with the standard duality argument to derive optimal error estimates in the L2-norm for the unknowns, which are novel for the NSD equations within the DG framework and are supported by numerical simulations demonstrating the scheme's efficiency.
item.dc:creator: Sweta Chakraborty, Deepjyoti Goswami, Saumya Bajpai

item.title: A locally conservative LDG method for the evolutionary Navier-Stokes-Darcy coupled problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.31073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes and investigates a local discontinuous Galerkin (LDG) method for the evolutionary Navier-Stokes-Darcy coupled problem representing the interaction between incompressible flows and porous media flows through the Beavers-Joseph-Saffman interface conditions. A fully discrete numerical scheme has been proposed and analyzed employing backward Euler temporal discretization and a locally conservative LDG scheme for the space discretization. The well-posedness of the numerical scheme has been obtained under a small data condition. Optimal a priori error estimates have been proven in the energy norm, as well as the L2-norm for t>0. Numerical experiments ensure the efficiency of the theoretical results
item.dc:creator: Sweta Chakraborty, Deepjyoti Goswami, Saumya Bajpai

item.title: Expressive Shallow Networks for Physics-Informed Learning: Why Curvature-Aware Optimization and FP64 Are Not Enough
item.description: arXiv:2611.28393v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often struggle with high-frequency and high-order partial differential equations (PDEs) due to optimization stiffness and spectral bias, despite possessing sufficient approximation capacity. Existing remedies, including modified feature representations, domain decomposition, higher floating-point precision, and curvature-aware optimizers, can improve convergence but largely act as workarounds for optimization difficulties arising from deep architectures rather than addressing their underlying source. We investigate Physics-Informed Shallow Universal Polynomial Networks (PI-SUPNs), which replace deep nonlinear compositions with learnable polynomial expansions, retaining high approximation capacity within a shallow computational graph. On a high-frequency Helmholtz benchmark, PI-SUPNs are the only architecture to successfully recover the solution, while all competing models fail even under FP64 precision and curvature-aware optimization. However, experiments on higher vibrational modes of a fourth-order Euler-Bernoulli beam reveal that architectural improvements alone are insufficient: accurate solutions require the combination of PI-SUPNs, FP64 precision, and curvature-aware optimization.
